newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps-Gas oil down, supplies overhang.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps-Gas oil down, supplies overhang.

text.p: The Singapore gas oil swaps slipped further at midday on Friday with an overhang of supplies and crude losses pushing the market lower, brokers said.
IPE Brent futures ended lower on Thursday, settling at 40 cents lower at $18.32 a barrel.
Traders said unsold prompt gas oil supplies were flooding the market.
They cited the eight physical offers from five sellers on Thursday as eveidence of the current soft market.
June gas oil swaps were quoted at $24.30/$24.50 per barrel while July was at $24.40/$24.55, down 15 and 20 cents from Thursday's quotes respectively, brokers said.
On Thursday, prompt gas oil was traded at 20 cents below its previous day's quote at $24.30.
They added that arbitrage cargoes from the West threatened to push prices lower while regional demand remained thin.
Up to four 60,000 to 80,000 tonnes tankers from the Mediterranean and Black Sea is expected to head to Asia for arrival in early July.
Brokers said June jet/gas oil regrade widened to -0.45/-0.50 cents, from Thursday's -0.30/-0.10 cents.
Traders attributed the softer regrade quotes to lower physical jet fuel prices. Jet fuel traded lower at $24.05.
Fuel oil swaps were also indicated lower. Brokers attributed the overall bearish sentiment in the swaps market to overnight crude losses.
June swaps was quoted at $100.00/$100.75 down from $100.50/$101.25.
July was quoted at $98.50/$99.50 down from $99.00/$99.75.
